Worked example: a name-cleaning line added to Harvest Lane's HL · Form order → Sheet Zap.

StepApp · event · transformInputRenamed to
2Formatter · Text · Trim WhitespaceName pill (step 1)Trim name
3Formatter · Text · LowercaseStep 2 outputLower name
4Formatter · Text · CapitalizeStep 3 outputCapitalise name
5Formatter · Text · Split Text, separator: space, segment: FirstStep 4 outputFirst name
6Formatter · Text · Split Text, separator: space, segment: LastStep 4 outputLast name
7Sheets · Create Spreadsheet Rowfirst_name ← step 5, last_name ← step 6Save row

The Lowercase step is there because Capitalize may leave "MAMA KEMI" in capitals; check your own test, and drop it if Capitalize already fixes the rest of each word.

Inputfirst_namelast_name
" mrs ADEBAYO "MrsAdebayo
"tunde bakare"TundeBakare
"MAMA KEMI"MamaKemi

Formatter steps use no tasks, so the Zap still costs one task per form response. Note in your log that a three-word name such as "Ngozi Ada Okafor" loses its middle name with First/Last.
mistakes: Splitting before trimming, so the leading spaces make the first segment empty.
Mapping the raw Name pill from step 1 into the sheet instead of the split outputs.
Assuming Capitalize lowercases the rest of the word without testing "MAMA KEMI".
Leaving every step named "Formatter", so nobody can tell which output is which.
b.pass: All three test names appear in the sheet as Mrs / Adebayo, Tunde / Bakare and Mama / Kemi in separate columns, with no leading or trailing spaces.
b.redo: Send it back if any name keeps stray spaces or capitals, sits in one column, or the sheet was mapped from the raw trigger pill.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's nine-step order Zap, HL · Form order → Sheet + alert, with Tomatoes (crate) at 12500 in Products.

Build: exactly the solved problem: Clean phone (NG, international format), Clean date (YYYY-MM-DD, Africa/Lagos), Look up price (Products, column name, stop if not found), Delivery fee (Bodija, Mokola, Ring Road 1500; Challenge 2000; fallback 2500), Total formula, Format Currency (NGN), Create Orders row (total from step 6), Send email.

Three tests, checked by hand:

#OrderHand calculationSheet totalEmail shows
12 × Tomatoes (crate), Bodija2 × 12500 + 1500 = 2650026500₦26,500.00
21 × Tomatoes (crate), Apete (new area)1 × 12500 + 2500 (fallback) = 1500015000₦15,000.00
—Tolu changes Tomatoes (crate) to 14000 in Products
33 × Tomatoes (crate), Mokola3 × 14000 + 1500 = 4350043500₦43,500.00

Checks: rows 1 and 2 still show unit_price 12500 after the change; row 3 shows 14000. The total column is right-aligned and a quick =SUM over it works, proving it holds numbers. Phones read +2348031234567; dates read 2026-10-06.

Log: 9 steps; transforms used: Format Phone Number, Date/Time Format, Lookup Table (fallback 2500), Spreadsheet-Style Formula, Format Currency. Tasks per order: read from Zap history (the app steps: lookup, row, email).
mistakes: Saving step 7's ₦ text into the total column, so =SUM returns 0.
Changing the price before the first two orders, so the 'only later orders change' test proves nothing.
No fallback value, so the new-area order gets a blank fee and a wrong total.
Mapping the raw phone or date pill from step 1 instead of the cleaned step 2 and 3 outputs.
s.pass: Three orders with hand calculations that match the sheet, a numeric total column, ₦ formatting only in the email, the fallback fee on the new area, and the new price only on the order placed after the change.
s.redo: Send it back if totals don't match the hand maths, the sheet stores formatted currency, or the price-change test was run in the wrong order.

g.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's 6 p.m. summary using option 2 (Schedule plus a Summary tab).

Summary tab (row 1 headers: label, order_count, order_value; row 2 values). In 0.4's Orders, created_at is column B and total is column I:

A2: today
B2: =COUNTIFS(Orders!B:B, ">="&TODAY())
C2: =SUMIFS(Orders!I:I, Orders!B:B, ">="&TODAY())

Zap: HL · 6pm summary.

StepSettings
1 · Schedule by Zapier · Every DayTime 6 p.m.; account time zone Africa/Lagos
2 · Sheets · Lookup Spreadsheet RowWorksheet Summary; lookup column label; value today
3 · Formatter · Numbers · Format CurrencyInput: order_value; NGN
4 · Gmail · Send EmailSubject: Harvest Lane today · [order_count] orders · [step 3 output]

Sample email (test day):

Subject: Harvest Lane today · 7 orders · ₦184,500.00

Orders today: 7
Value today: ₦184,500.00
Full list: the Orders tab, filtered to today.

Check: filter Orders to today and add up by hand: 7 rows, 184500. Matches.

Two lines for a client: "I'd give a client option 2. It costs two tasks a day whatever the volume, and the owner can see the same numbers in the sheet at any time; Digest needs a task per order and must be included in their plan."

Submit: the Summary formulas, the Zap outline, a screenshot of the email that arrived at 18:00 (from Zap history: the run time), your hand check, and the two lines.
mistakes: Account time zone left on UTC, so the email arrives at 7 p.m. Lagos time or counts the wrong day.
SUMIFS over a column of ₦-formatted text, so the value is 0.
Testing by clicking Test step at noon and never waiting for a real 18:00 run.
The two-line recommendation names an option but gives no reason (tasks, visibility, plan).
g.pass: Zap history shows a scheduled run at 18:00 Lagos time, the email's count and total match a hand check of that day's rows, and two lines justify the chosen option.
g.redo: Send it back if the numbers don't match the sheet, the email only arrived from a manual test, or the recommendation has no reasoning.
